correctness.rationale: Defined graph and ordinary cut convention explicitly; Alexander dual has complete 1-skeleton, 6n path triangles, n tetrahedral squares and no larger faces. Explicit 5n-by-5n unimodular minor (block lower triangular after separating distance-two chords and square triangles) and primitive tetrahedron-boundary sublattice determine integral H1 and acyclicity above. Alexander duality, connectivity and Whitehead give the wedge. Oriented fixed-simplex traces and vertex-permutation sign give the complete character. Standalone verify.py executed successfully n=5..16 for 504 group elements, and independently computes full cut-complex signed traces n=5..7; finite checks supplement rather than prove the general theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The graph-wide edge-disjoint-square theorem is not applicable: each antipodal edge lies in two squares. The circular-ladder theorem treats an untwisted graph and nonequivariant homotopy. Total-cut results do not govern connected-triple cut complexes.

value.rationale: The primary literature identifies cut complexes of Möbius ladders as a natural open direction. An all-width dihedral action on the ordinary three-cut complex yields explicit rotation and inequivalent reflection-axis character values and invariant dimension floor((n-3)/2), contrasting with quadratic nonequivariant Betti number. Nonequivariant wedge ranks or unrelated total-cut/independence representations do not imply this finer structural result.
